details: The cryptocurrency market, including Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and XRP, experienced significant declines on October 7-8, 2026. This downturn is largely attributed to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which have driven international oil prices higher and reignited fears of energy-driven inflation. Simultaneously, US Treasury yields have surged to a 24-year high, making non-yielding assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive to investors. Federal Reserve minutes released on October 7 pointed to the possibility of another rate increase this year, with an 85% probability priced in for a December hike, signaling continued monetary tightening efforts to combat inflation. This macro pressure, combined with over $700 million in leveraged long liquidations on October 7 and an additional $550 million on October 8, has created a bearish sentiment, reducing risk appetite in the crypto space.
title: Crypto Market Faces Pressure Amid Rising Oil, Yields, and Fed Hike Fears

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its October 8, 2026 Global Financial Stability Report, noted the rapid growth of the tokenized market for real-world assets (RWA), which has quadrupled to approximately $65.1 billion since early last year. Despite this growth, the IMF identified significant bottlenecks, including unclear legal rights, inadequate regulatory rules, a lack of interoperability between platforms, and the absence of a secure, universal settlement asset. The report indicated that tokenized markets remain relatively small, fragmented, and less liquid than traditional markets, while also being more volatile. Interestingly, over half of tokenized stock trading occurs outside traditional market hours, and about 80% of trades involve less than one full share, pointing to investor demand for continuous and fractional access.
title: IMF Highlights Growth and Bottlenecks in Tokenized Markets

details: The Bank of Russia introduced new mandatory cryptocurrency disclosure requirements, effective July 1, 2027. Commercial banks and financial institutions will now be required to explicitly include client cryptocurrency balances, mining revenue, and income from digital asset sales in standardized account certificates. This move aims to enhance transparency across the domestic financial system. Concurrently, Russia has approved its first crypto exchanges and custodians under new rules, legalizing crypto trading, mining, and exchange services under strict central bank oversight. While retail trading for assets like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and and USDT is permitted, cryptocurrencies remain prohibited for domestic payments. Furthermore, draft prudential rules cap banks' combined risk from cryptocurrencies and foreign digital instruments at 1% of their capital.
title: Bank of Russia Mandates Crypto Disclosure, Approves Exchanges
